findings.text: the per-row ladder supports a persistent above-gate exact-mode mismatch but not a resolution-independent floor: diverted exact sup/RMS runs 0.447979/0.490527, 0.299535/0.297526, 0.120879/0.073817, 0.149589/0.223683 and 0.120138/0.165754, while reactor-static exact ends 0.025369/0.029156 at 1000 and 0.016333/0.019834 at 2500; the non-monotonic sequence and 20 to 36 percent finest-step changes do not identify an asymptotic constant.

the support/profile-moment attribution carried by the plasma response is supported: independent recomputation over all twenty NPZ archives finds zero non-finite moment elements, maximum exterior absolute disagreement 5.68434188608e-14 Wb, maximum map recomposition closure 5.68434188608e-14 Wb, and each stored plasma-response absolute sup error equals the map's raw absolute sup error; the shared Green operator still limits this to component attribution rather than kernel validation.

a ladder-wide claim that the diverted exact mismatch field is dominated by vertical displacement of the support-current centroid is not supported. Centre-weighted support current reproduces the stored analytic centroid to 0.12 mm; at 110 and 300 requested cells the measured vertical centroid shifts are -35.41 and -21.44 mm and a vertical-gradient template explains 0.886 and 0.775 of mismatch variance, but at 500 the vertical template explains 0.036, and at 1000 and 2500 radial-only fits explain 0.430 and 0.506 versus vertical-only 0.269 and 0.141; at 2500 the radial centroid shift is 5.73 mm versus 4.72 mm vertically.

the committed audit checks that detected_in_both_norms agrees with recomputation but never requires that value to be true, and it does not recompute exterior_mismatch, plasma_response_mismatch, scaled_current_l1_relative_error or failure_component; it can therefore print PASS after the declared displacement control stops raising mismatch or after the component-attribution fields drift, so the archive audit is a consistency check rather than a durable guard for the two scientific claims.
